name: Leg press
pattern: Machine squat: the back is supported while the legs bend and press a sled or platform away.
setup: Sit with your back and hips flat on the pad.
Feet hip to shoulder width in the middle of the platform, toes slightly out.
Hold the handles, brace, and release the safety catches.

steps.text: Legs almost straight, knees soft, not locked.
Bend your knees and let the platform come toward you, knees in line with your toes.
Stop at about a 90° knee bend, or just before your hips start to lift off the pad.
Push through your whole foot back to the top.

cues.cue: Hips and lower back stay glued to the pad.
cues.why: Going so deep that the pelvis tucks rounds the lower back under load.

cues.cue: Knees follow your toes, never inward.
cues.why: Keeps the load even across the knee.

cues.cue: About 90° at the knee for most people.
cues.why: Quad activity peaks around 90° knee bend; going deeper mostly adds knee-cap pressure.

cues.cue: Higher feet for more glutes, lower feet for more quads.
cues.why: High foot placement raised glute activity; low placement raised quad activity in most studies.

cues.cue: Stop just short of locking your knees.
cues.why: Keeps tension on the muscles and avoids snapping the knee straight under a heavy sled.

breathing: Breathe in as the platform comes down, out as you press.

tempo.note: Lower in about 2 seconds; never let the sled drop.

mistakes.name: Hips curl off the pad
mistakes.looks: At the bottom the tailbone lifts and the lower back rounds.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the depth or move your feet higher on the platform.
mistakes.why: Hip flexion has run out, so the spine bends instead.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: The knees drift toward each other as you press.
mistakes.fix: Push your knees out over your toes; use less weight.
mistakes.why: Weak hip abductors let the thighs roll in.

mistakes.name: Knees snap locked
mistakes.looks: The knees straighten hard or bend slightly backward at the top.
mistakes.fix: Stop with a soft bend in the knee.
mistakes.why: A locked knee carries the whole sled on the joint.

mistakes.name: Heels lift off the platform
mistakes.looks: Only the balls of the feet stay on the platform at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Move your feet higher and press through your heels.
mistakes.why: Feet too low for your ankle range; load shifts onto the knee and toes.

safety: Set the safety catches and never push the sled with your hands on your knees.
Lower-back pain: keep the range shallow so your hips never leave the pad.
Knee pain: work from about 90° to nearly straight; deeper knee bend raises knee-cap pressure.

variants.change: Hack squat: standing with your back on an angled pad; shins travel further forward, more knee bend and more quads.
Belt squat: load hangs from a hip belt, trunk upright, spine unloaded; squat keyframes.
Pendulum squat: the pad swings on an arc; deep knee bend with an upright trunk.
One leg at a time: half the load, the other foot rests on the frame.
Seated horizontal press: trunk nearly upright, same leg angles.
Band leg press lying on the floor: pull the knee to the chest and push the foot out against the band.
Smith leg press: lying under the bar, feet press it up; same leg keyframes, trunk flat.

subtypes.name: Hack squat
subtypes.change: You stand on the platform with your back and shoulders under pads that slide on rails tilted back; it moves like a squat.

subtypes.name: Belt squat
subtypes.change: Standing on a platform with the weight hung from a belt at the hips; upright squat.

metrics.label: Knee bend
metrics.good: 85-100 at the bottom, 5-15 at the top

metrics.label: Knee inside the foot line (front view)

motion.basis: Knee range (about 90° to near straight) and foot-height effects from martinfuentes2020 and escamilla2001b; seat back assumed at 45° (trunk -45) for a 45° sled. Hip angles estimated from the seat and knee angles. Hack and belt squat keyframes estimated from the squat pattern.

sources.cite: Martín-Fuentes I, Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. Evaluation of the lower limb muscles' electromyographic activity during the leg press exercise and its variants: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2020;17(13):4626.
